findings.reason: the node's whole evidence is one real run on the new backend, and a dispatch that is refused or routes elsewhere leaves it either blocked on a command form that cannot work or reporting a `clive` run as the omp arm.
findings.text: the done-when says the pilot node is "dispatched with `--set backend=omp-local`", but `--set` overrides flight keys after file layers (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1377`, "Override one flight key after file layers … A path naming a backend or role no config layer defines is refused") and the flight schema has no `backend` key — it has `default_backend`, `local_backend` and `backends` (`reckon/_flight_schema.py:205-210`); backend selection is `--backend` / `--local` (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1199`, `:1432`)

findings.reason: an unfenced or resumed run records the treatment flag while receiving no anchored server and no disallowed `Edit`, so §8 would split the population by a flag that does not describe what ran and would score the arm on contaminated runs.
findings.text: the plan reads the `anchored_edit` key "where a run home is seeded … beside `_seed_worker_mcp_settings`", but that function is called only when the dialect is claude, the run is fenced, the run home's `settings.json` did not already exist, and `worker_mcp_servers is not None` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:267-272`, called from `reckon/_backends.py:2383-2397` with `None` when no flight config is resolved), while the plan sets `anchored_edit: true` on the run record unconditionally

findings.reason: §7 is declared to be built on what §6 settled, so an empty §6 result still promotes and hands the dependent node a contract it cannot implement.
findings.text: the investigation's done-when is satisfied by a note that "marks any item it could not settle as unsettled with the reason", so a node that settles none of the five items passes, and nothing in the measure can fail

findings.reason: the empty-read failure is the shape §1 already records once (60 codex runs, 594 `file_change` items and zero failures, judged "not believable as a measurement"), and without a fixture that must trip the refusal nothing shows the parser's refusal path executes.
findings.text: the node declares a positive control for the parser (non-zero totals on a known-healthy stream) but no negative control, though the section states the guard it needs: "a stream format this parser does not recognise is a refusal, never a run read as empty"

findings.reason: the adopt/no-adopt verdict is the plan's only output, and a query that returns a uniform column for both arms would satisfy the stated done-when unchanged.
findings.text: the measurement record asserts a per-arm table and a verdict but names no control showing the query can distinguish arms, while §1 records a census of the same shape reporting zero codex edit failures and calls it "not believable as a measurement"
